identity.title: Network Sparsity Unlocks the Scaling Potential of Deep Reinforcement Learning

problem.claim: Scaling deep reinforcement learning models effectively is difficult because of network pathologies during training.

contributions.claim: Introduces static network sparsity via simple one-shot random pruning before training.
Reports that sparse networks provide greater parameter efficiency and stronger resistance to plasticity loss and gradient interference than naively scaled dense networks.
Extends the evaluation to visual and streaming reinforcement learning scenarios.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their approach by using static sparsity alone, rather than more complex modifications, to unlock scaling beyond dense counterparts with state-of-the-art architectures.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that one-shot randomly pruned sparse networks can outperform dense counterparts with state-of-the-art architectures in scaling potential.
The authors report higher parameter efficiency for expressivity and greater resistance to plasticity loss and gradient interference in sparse networks than in naively scaled dense networks.
The authors report consistent benefits of network sparsity in visual and streaming reinforcement learning scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: Scaling deep reinforcement learning is hindered by training-time network pathologies, motivating interventions such as periodic reset and layer normalization.
The paper proposes static network sparsity alone as an alternative route to scaling beyond dense architectures.
Sparsity is created by randomly removing a predetermined percentage of weights once before training.
The authors associate sparsity with improved parameter efficiency and resistance to plasticity loss and gradient interference.
The evaluation is extended to visual and streaming reinforcement learning, where benefits are reported as consistent.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a simple intervention, one-shot random pruning, to specific scaling-related properties including parameter efficiency, plasticity-loss resistance, and reduced gradient interference.

lessons.interpretation: A compact abstract can make a method claim more informative by pairing the intervention with hypothesized or analyzed mechanisms and concrete failure modes.
lessons.application: When presenting a model intervention, state its minimal operational recipe and connect it to the particular training pathologies or resource trade-offs it is intended to address.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the abstract lacks evidence or analysis connecting the intervention to those mechanisms.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify pruning percentages, benchmarks, model sizes, quantitative gains, or evaluation protocols.
The basis for the claimed consistency across visual and streaming reinforcement learning scenarios is not detailed.
The abstract does not state a limitation of existing understanding or approaches distinct from the general scaling difficulty.
